title: Gorgeous Front Hand Mandala Mehndi Design for Front Hand
descriptionParagraphs: A striking front hand mehndi design tailored for the palm, featuring crescent motif and bracelet cuff. Rated as Expert, this pattern is perfect for everyday.

The palm has the thickest skin on the hand, so henna stains darkest here. Keep the hand open and relaxed while the paste dries so the lines do not crack or smudge. This is a detailed pattern usually done by an experienced artist; allow plenty of time and work in small sections.
The palm is the traditional placement for mehndi and gives the darkest stain on the body. A round mandala in the centre of the palm, often called a tikki, is one of the oldest and best-known layouts.

Application tips: Leave the paste on for at least four to six hours; the longer it stays, the deeper the stain. Dab a lemon and sugar mixture on the dried paste to keep it moist and stuck to the skin.

image.alt: Front Hand Mandala mehndi design for front hand — gorgeous henna pattern

faq.q: Is black henna safe?
faq.a: Natural henna is never black. Products sold as black henna often contain PPD, a hair-dye chemical that can cause skin reactions, so they are best avoided.

faq.q: How can I make my mehndi darker?
faq.a: Leave the paste on longer, seal it with lemon and sugar, keep the skin warm, and avoid water for the first day after removing the paste.

faq.q: Should I do a patch test before applying mehndi?
faq.a: Yes. Apply a small amount of the paste to the inner arm and wait 24 hours, especially if you have sensitive skin or are using a new cone.

title: Artistic Front Hand Ribbon Weave Mehndi Design for Front Hand
descriptionParagraphs: A luxurious front hand mehndi design tailored for the palm, featuring petal arrangement and wave pattern. Rated as Hard, this pattern is perfect for everyday.

The palm has the thickest skin on the hand, so henna stains darkest here. Keep the hand open and relaxed while the paste dries so the lines do not crack or smudge. This pattern needs steady pressure control and fine line work, so it is best attempted after practising simpler designs.
